title: Fatal shooting by police probed: [MET Edition]
article: Seven Special Investigations Unit officers are probing the death of a 27-year-old man shot by police responding to a burglary in a Newmarket home yesterday afternoon.
"It's very scary. I've never seen anything like this before," said Attila Vinczer, who lives about a block away from the Southwind Court home, in the Mulock Dr. and Leslie St. area.
Vinczer was in the kitchen with his father and his son Ryan, 4, when a convoy of police cars raced down Premier Place at about 4 15 p.m.
"A minute or so afterwards, we heard a loud bang and I knew somebody had been shot," he added.
The shooting occurred at a two-storey brick home that sits on a lot surrounded by tall trees.
Vinczer said a couple who live at the home have two university- age children.
Police said officers were responding to a report of a break-in at the house. Police were confronted by a man as they approached the house, SIU said.
"Upon arrival, officers had a confrontation with a male suspect and as a result the individual was fatally shot by one of our members," said Insp. Mark Brown of York Regional Police.
"He succumbed to his injuries a short time after the shooting."
The victim's identity hasn't been released.
York Regional Police shot and killed Shelton McKenzie during an April 13 home invasion. A 40-year-old man was also shot dead by York police responding to a domestic dispute on Jan. 11.
Shaheen Kamadia received a $3.3 million wrongful-death settlement after a York officer shot and killed her son in 1996.
